text:
### Observed differences

- A10 became much more common: it appears in about 72% of traces in the later window, up from about 21%, and its mean occurrences per trace rose from 0.23 to 0.78. [OCC005]
- A02, A04, A06 and A08 became less common: trace participation fell from about 25% to 11%, 23% to 6%, 24% to 5% and 31% to 9% respectively. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004]
- A30, A31, A36, A37 and A38 were repeated about 3.5 times per trace earlier (recurrence about 70% of traces) and now occur about once per trace (recurrence about 1–2%), while still appearing in every trace. [OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009, OCC010]
- A10's successors changed from many activities to mainly A19 (about 44%) and A20 (about 45%); A38's main successor changed from A30 (about 70%) to A25 (about 98%); A41's main successor changed from A19/A20 to A10 (about 70%). [DIR004, DIR006, DIR007]
- A10 now co-occurs with A14, A15, A30, A31, A36, A37, A38, A41, A46 and A47 in about 72% of traces, up from about 21%. [REL001, REL002, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012]
- The repeated activities A30, A31, A36, A37, A38 changed from being interleaved with A14, A15, A19 and A20 (interleaved in about 70–82% of co-occurring traces) to a single pass: A14 now precedes them in about 98% of traces, A15 in about 63%, and A19/A20 in about 49%. [REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL024, REL025, REL026, REL027, REL028, REL029, REL030, REL031, REL032]
- A10 now precedes A30, A31, A36, A37 and A38 in about 65% of traces (up from about 3%), and A41 now precedes A10 in about 64% of traces (up from 11%). [REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010]
- A10's mean position moved earlier (relative position from about 0.49 to 0.34), and A10–A19 and A10–A20 are now adjacent (lag 1) in about 97–100% of co-occurring traces, whereas earlier their lags were spread over 1–5 steps. [POS001, LAG001, LAG002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the process changed from a repeated, interleaved execution of a group of activities (A30, A31, A36, A37, A38) to a single execution of each in a fixed order, with A10 becoming a common step between A41 and the A19/A20/A30… group. The number of qualifying items (116) is far above the 1.16 expected by chance, and the signs are direct and consistent: the repetition of A30/A31/A36/A37/A38 dropped from about 3.5 to about 1 occurrence per trace [OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009, OCC010]; the interleaving between these activities and A14/A15/A19/A20 was replaced by a single pass with A14 now preceding them [REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL024, REL025, REL026, REL027, REL028, REL029, REL030, REL031, REL032]; A10's participation rose from about 21% to about 72% and it now sits between A41 and the A19/A20/A30… group [OCC005, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, DIR004, DIR007]; and A10's position moved earlier [POS001]. A limitation is that the evidence cannot determine whether A10 was added to the process or an existing rare path became dominant, and some lag details rest on very few traces in one window (e.g., LAG013, LAG015, LAG017, LAG020–LAG022 have only 2–3 supporting traces after), so the precise ordering of those pairs is weak.

Other differences: A02, A04, A06 and A08 became less common [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004]; A38's main successor changed from A30 to A25 [DIR006].

An important competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that the change reflects a shift in case mix rather than a modification of the process itself.
